rationale: Evidence: all 60 development trials across the three tracks ended off_track with zero completions. Max error sits at about 0.060 to 0.064 m on every design, which is the off-track limit, so the robot leaves the tape by a consistent overshoot. Iteration 1 (kp 4.0, kd 0.5, base 1.4, sensor y 0.03) gave the best scores and the most oval progress (0.20). Iteration 2 lowered kd to 0.2, kp to 3.0, base to 1.2 and moved the sensors to y 0.05. That cut oscillation but lost progress on oval (0.11) and slalom (0.10), so the forward sensor offset and weaker gains probably cost more than they saved. Iteration 2 also reported zero line losses on oval, so the wider 16 mm sensor spread is working and I keep it. Changes: (1) return the sensor row to y 0.03, the setting that gave the best progress; (2) kp 4.0 to 4.5 for a stronger correction per unit of offset; (3) kd 0.5 to 0.6, a small increase in damping against the faster response; (4) ki 0.0 to 0.3. A fixed left/right motor mismatch acts as a steady bias, and a small integral term can cancel it so the robot stops sitting off-centre on straights; the integral is clamped at +/-2, so the added turn is bounded. base_speed stays at 1.4 because survival still matters more than speed. Expected result: progress above 0.2 on all tracks and max_error somewhat below 0.06, with steering_oscillation near 0.12 or lower. Hypotheses to check next: (H1) if steering_oscillation rises above about 0.2, kp is too high for kd and kd should go to about 1.0; (H2) if max_error still reaches 0.06 on the same bend in every trial, the cause is the speed-to-curvature limit and base_speed should drop to about 1.0; (H3) if the integral pushes the robot off-line, set ki back to 0. Measurements wanted per track: completion, progress, completion_time, max_error, rms_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation and noise_robustness.
